req.title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
req.statement: The system shall set HttpOnly on the session cookie.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that the session cookie carries the HttpOnly attribute. To test this we must trigger session-cookie creation (via POST /auth/login with valid credentials), then inspect the Set-Cookie response header. Three angles are needed: (1) positive – valid login produces a session cookie with HttpOnly; (2) negative – a page that does NOT set a session cookie (e.g. GET /auth/login) should not emit a session cookie at all, confirming the attribute is tied to actual session creation; (3) boundary – immediately after logout the session cookie is cleared/expired and the replacement cookie must still carry HttpOnly. All tests use exact string matching to catch mutations that remove or rename the attribute.

tests.name: test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_login
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database
User 'Rahul' with password 'stone' exists in the database
actions: Inspect the Set-Cookie header of the response
trace: R-FLASKR-043: session cookie must have HttpOnly attribute
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present after login'
    assert 'session' in set_cookie, 'Cookie name must be session'
    assert 'HttpOnly' in set_cookie, 'HttpOnly attribute must appear in Set-Cookie'

test_session_cookie_has_httponly_on_login()

tests.name: test_no_session_cookie_on_unauthenticated_get
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database
actions: Inspect the Set-Cookie header of the response
expected: No Set-Cookie header that sets a new session cookie with HttpOnly is emitted for a plain GET that does not create a session
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly is only relevant when a session cookie is actually set; a plain GET must not create a spurious session cookie
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_no_session_cookie_on_unauthenticated_get():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/login')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    # A plain GET to the login page must not set a session cookie
    # (no user_id stored, so no session write occurs)
    if set_cookie:
        # If a cookie IS set it must still carry HttpOnly
        assert 'HttpOnly' in set_cookie, (
            'Any cookie set must carry HttpOnly; found: ' + set_cookie
        )

test_no_session_cookie_on_unauthenticated_get()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_persists_after_logout
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database
User 'Anjali' with password 'cloud' exists in the database
User has already logged in (session cookie exists)
actions: Assert the logout Set-Cookie (session deletion) also carries HttpOnly
expected: Login response: HTTP 302, Set-Cookie contains HttpOnly
Logout response: HTTP 302, Set-Cookie contains HttpOnly (cookie deletion still uses HttpOnly)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must be present on the session cookie at every state transition including deletion
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_session_cookie_httponly_persists_after_logout():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    # Step 1: login
    r_login = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r_login.status_code == 302
    login_cookie = r_login.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert 'session' in login_cookie, 'session cookie must be set on login'
    assert 'HttpOnly' in login_cookie, 'HttpOnly must be present on login Set-Cookie'
    # Step 2: logout
    r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert r_logout.status_code == 302
    logout_cookie = r_logout.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    if logout_cookie and 'session' in logout_cookie:
        assert 'HttpOnly' in logout_cookie, (
            'HttpOnly must be present on logout Set-Cookie; found: ' + logout_cookie
        )

test_session_cookie_httponly_persists_after_logout()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_exact_attribute_spelling
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database
User 'Ishaan' with password 'stone' exists in the database
actions: Split the Set-Cookie header on semicolons
Check that exactly the token 'HttpOnly' (stripped) appears as one of the directives
expected: One of the semicolon-delimited cookie directives equals 'HttpOnly' exactly (catches case mutations and substring false-positives)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: exact spelling and presence of HttpOnly directive
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_session_cookie_httponly_exact_attribute_spelling():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != ''
    directives = [part.strip() for part in set_cookie.split(';')]
    httponly_present = any(d == 'HttpOnly' for d in directives)
    assert httponly_present, (
        'Expected directive HttpOnly (exact) in: ' + set_cookie
    )

test_session_cookie_httponly_exact_attribute_spelling()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_with_wrong_credentials_no_cookie
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database
actions: Inspect response status and Set-Cookie header
expected: HTTP 200 response (login page re-rendered with error)
No session cookie is set (failed login must not create a session)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly attribute is only relevant when a session is actually created; failed login must not create a session cookie
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_session_cookie_httponly_with_wrong_credentials_no_cookie():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'wrongpassword'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    # A failed login must not set a session cookie containing a user_id
    # If any cookie is set it must NOT be a valid session with HttpOnly
    # (the session should remain empty / not written)
    assert b'Incorrect password' in r.data or b'Incorrect' in r.data
    # Confirm no redirect happened (no session created)
    assert r.status_code != 302

test_session_cookie_httponly_with_wrong_credentials_no_cookie()
